full_judgment:
2. Short facts necessary for disposal of this petition are that respondent Nos. 1-25 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 26 of 1991 in the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Chandpur for partition of the Suit land measuring an area of 1.42 acres. The petitioners who were defendant Nos. 6-9, 26 and 31-34 filed written statement, but eventually they did not contest the suit and the suit was decreed in preliminary form on 28.11.2002 on contest against defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and ex-parte against the other defendants including the petitioners. Against the said decree, the petitioners filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) giving rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2003 Miscellaneous case was rejected on 15.04.2004 as being not maintainable. In the order, the learned Joint District Judge observed that since final decree was not drawn till then the petitioner could seek saham in the partition suit which was still in the form of preliminary decree and that there was scope to amend or alter the saham of the parties allotted in the preliminary decree. Thereafter, the petitioners filed an application for giving them saham. The trial Court rejected the prayer on the ground that after giving saham to the plaintiffs there was no land from which saham could be given. The same view has been affirmed by the District Judge in Civil Revision No. 10 of 2006 filed under section 115(2) of the Code. Being aggrieved by the said order of the District Judge, the petitioner, the petitioner preferred civil revision before the High Court Division being No. 3264 of 2009 under section 115(4) of the code. The High Court Division also took the same view at the same time it observed: 

 "In the instant case, since the decree is in preliminary form and final decree is yet to be drawn up, the petitioner can prefer appeal against the preliminary decree. On perusal of the record it is also apparent that the petitioners suffered for no fault of them but in view of the provision of law and the decision referred above, I am of the opinion that their proper remedy lies in the Court of appeal against the preliminary decree which can be filed any time before final decree is drawn up"
